patients.summary: Marketing manager with Hashimoto thyroiditis on levothyroxine and adolescent anorexia nervosa in remission who joins in 2019. Infertility care at outside gynecology brings Asherman syndrome after a myomectomy, then a prolactinoma that grows to compress the chiasm and responds to cabergoline, primary ovarian insufficiency, later weight loss, and an ED visit for psychogenic urinary retention after the practice last saw her.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
30-year-old woman new to the practice. Moved her care here after her previous office closed its panel; records requested.

Thyroid: told she had Hashimoto's about ten years ago, on levothyroxine 75 mcg each morning ever since, no dose changes in years. Feels well on it. No palpitations, no cold intolerance, energy fine.

Eating disorder history: anorexia nervosa as a teenager, treated with outpatient therapy and family-based work in high school. She describes it as long behind her and says she eats normally now; weight has been steady for years. We agreed to keep an eye on it the way we would any chronic history, without making it the focus of every visit.

PSH: none. Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily. Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: mother treated for major depression; maternal aunt with an autoimmune thyroid problem; sister has PCOS.
Social: marketing manager. Married. Never smoked. A glass of wine once or twice a week. Walks most evenings.
Gyn: regular cycles. Sees an outside gynecologist. Last Pap last year, normal per her report.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well appearing, pleasant. Vitals as charted. Thyroid normal size, no nodules, nontender. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Skin normal. Mood and affect appropriate.

A/P
1. Hashimoto thyroiditis, stable on levothyroxine 75 mcg. TSH today; continue current dose if in range.
2. History of anorexia nervosa, in remission. BMI about 20.6. PHQ-9 2.
3. Health maintenance: baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening done today. Tdap given (last one she remembers was in college). Pap per her gynecologist; will confirm date from old records.

Follow up yearly, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wendy, all of your labs from Tuesday look good. Thyroid level is right where it should be on 75 mcg, so no change. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests and cholesterol are normal, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. See you next year.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present.
reports.conclusion: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

Includes problem list (Hashimoto thyroiditis; history of anorexia nervosa, adolescent), med list (levothyroxine 75 mcg daily), yearly TSH values all within range, an April 2018 Pap reported negative, and immunization record. Scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Old chart reviewed. Levothyroxine dose has been 75 mcg for the whole stretch with stable TSH. Eating disorder history documented in her teens, no recurrence noted in their notes. Pap April 2018 normal, next due 2021 by cytology alone. Nothing else to act on.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam, masked visit. She and her husband started trying for a pregnancy last month. Cycles regular, roughly every 28 days. No pelvic pain, no unusual bleeding. She has an appointment with her gynecologist this winter for a preconception visit.

Thyroid stable, no symptoms. Eating well, weight unchanged. Mood good, working from home since spring, says it suits her.

Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Thyroid without enlargement. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen benign. No edema.

Plan:
- Preconception: start folic acid 0.4 mg daily now. Thyroid needs a check early in any pregnancy because the dose usually goes up; she should call as soon as she has a positive test. TSH today.
- Flu vaccine given.
- PHQ-2 negative.
- Pap due next year by the old record; gynecology can do it.
Return in a year.

conditions.label: Asherman syndrome
conditions.note: Suspected intrauterine adhesions after hysteroscopic myomectomy; negative progesterone challenge.

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY PRACTICE - CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of service: 08/06/2021
Re: Wendy Schmidt, DOB 12/16/1988

Thank you for allowing us to participate in Ms. Schmidt's care. She is a 32-year-old G0 seen for absent menses. Before her hysteroscopic fibroid resection in February her cycles came like clockwork; she has not bled once in the six months since. She and her husband have been trying for a pregnancy for about a year without success.

PMH: Hashimoto thyroiditis on levothyroxine 75 mcg daily; history of anorexia nervosa, in remission.
PSH: hysteroscopic myomectomy, 2/2021.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: maternal aunt with autoimmune thyroid disease, mother with depression, sister with PCOS.
SH: never smoker, occasional alcohol, works in marketing.

Exam: vital signs normal. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. External genitalia, vagina and cervix normal; uterus normal size, mobile; adnexa without masses or tenderness.

Data: urine hCG negative in the office. Thyroid function and prolactin from this visit were within normal limits. She completed a 10-day progestin challenge with no withdrawal bleed.

Impression: secondary amenorrhea after intrauterine surgery with a negative progestin challenge and normal thyroid and prolactin results, most consistent with intrauterine adhesions (Asherman syndrome). Infertility of one year.

Plan: operative hysteroscopy for evaluation and lysis of adhesions, scheduling for September.

Allergies: NKDA. cc: primary care physician

conditions.label: Secondary amenorrhea
conditions.note: Menses returned October 2021 after hysteroscopic adhesiolysis.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. A lot has happened on the gyn side this year. The fibroid resection in February was followed by six months of no periods; her gynecologist (letter in chart from August) thought scar tissue and took her back for an operative hysteroscopy on 9/14 to cut adhesions. No operative report has come to us; per her they found and divided scar tissue. Her period came back in October and the next one is due now. Still trying to conceive, still on folic acid.

New: for about three weeks she has noticed milky fluid from both nipples, sometimes on her bra, sometimes when she showers. No lumps, no pain, no redness. Not breastfeeding, never pregnant. No headaches, no change in vision. No new medications.

Thyroid: no symptoms on 75 mcg.

Exam: vitals as charted. Thyroid not enlarged. Breasts: symmetric, no masses, no skin change, no axillary nodes; with gentle pressure a small amount of white milky fluid comes from multiple ducts on both sides. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft. Neuro grossly nonfocal.

Urine hCG negative in the office.

A/P
1. Bilateral milky nipple discharge, i.e. galactorrhea. Prolactin and TSH today. No meds that would explain it. Referring to endocrinology regardless of the number, given the fertility picture.
2. Secondary amenorrhea after myomectomy, adhesions lysed in September, cycles back. Off the active list.
3. Hashimoto: TSH today.
4. Prevention: flu shot today; CBC and CMP. PHQ-9 3.

Asked her to have gynecology send the hysteroscopy report.

documents.title: Prolactin result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Wendy, your prolactin came back at 31, a bit above the normal range. That level can cause milk production and it also matters for fertility, so it's good you're seeing endocrinology. They'll likely repeat it and may want imaging of the pituitary gland. Thyroid, blood counts and chemistry were all normal. The referral is in; you should get a call from their office.

documents.title: RE: Prolactin result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok. Is a pituitary problem serious? A little freaked out reading online.

documents.title: RE: Prolactin result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Very understandable. A mildly high prolactin has several causes and most of them are very treatable, including the small pituitary growths that are the most common one. Let's let the endocrinologist sort out which it is before worrying. Call me if you develop headaches or any change in your vision before then.

documents.title: Referral scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Endocrinology office called to confirm they received the referral. First available new consult 1/27/22. Patient aware and has the date.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group
New consultation, seen 1/27/2022
Referring: primary care
Reason: galactorrhea

HPI: 33F (age 33 next month) with autoimmune hypothyroidism on replacement and remote anorexia nervosa, recently treated by gynecology for post-myomectomy intrauterine adhesions, sent for milky discharge from both breasts for roughly 3 months. The fluid looks like milk. No breast pain, no lumps she can feel. Cycles have been regular since the September hysteroscopy.

Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: maternal aunt autoimmune thyroid disease; mother depression; sister PCOS.
Social: marketing, never smoker, alcohol 1-2/wk.

Exam: vitals unremarkable. Breasts without tenderness or palpable mass; milky discharge expressed readily from both sides.

Labs today: urine pregnancy negative. Prolactin 35 ng/mL (ref 4-23). TSH 2.5.

Assessment: hyperprolactinemia with galactorrhea, persistent on repeat (31 at PCP in November). Not explained by thyroid status or medications. Need to exclude a pituitary lesion.

Plan: MRI pituitary with and without contrast. Will call with results and discuss treatment.

cc: PCP

reports.study: MR Pituitary and Sella turcica WO and W contrast IV
reports.text:
Indication: hyperprolactinemia, galactorrhea.
Technique: thin-section sagittal and coronal T1 and coronal T2 images through the sella before and after IV gadolinium, including dynamic coronal post-contrast imaging.
Findings: There is a 6 x 5 mm focus of delayed enhancement relative to normal gland in the left aspect of the pituitary gland. The infundibulum is midline. The optic chiasm is normal in position and signal with clearance above the gland. The cavernous sinuses are symmetric without evidence of invasion; the cavernous carotid flow voids are normal. Sella is normal in size. Visualized brain is unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: 6 mm left-sided pituitary microadenoma. No mass effect on the optic chiasm. No cavernous sinus invasion.

documents.title: MRI pituitary
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Outside imaging center report received for MRI pituitary with and without contrast performed 2/8/2022 at the request of endocrinology. Impression: 6 mm left-sided pituitary microadenoma, chiasm clear, no cavernous sinus invasion. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Result review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: MRI shows a 6 mm microadenoma, fits a prolactinoma with her prolactin. Chiasm clear. Endocrinology ordered this and will manage; will confirm the plan with her.

documents.title: New medication from endo
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! The endocrinologist called after the MRI. She said it's a small prolactinoma and started me on cabergoline, half a pill twice a week (0.5 mg pills, so 0.25). I started Monday. She said I can keep trying to get pregnant and to call her if I get a positive test. Just letting you know since it's not on my list here.

documents.title: RE: New medication from endo
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. Cabergoline is the standard treatment and usually works well for these. Some people get a little nausea or lightheadedness the first few weeks; taking it at bedtime with a snack helps. We'll update your med list at your next visit. Could you ask her office to send us their notes going forward?

medications.sig: Take one-half tablet (0.25 mg) by mouth twice weekly

OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY PRACTICE - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 08/09/2022
Re: Wendy Schmidt, DOB 12/16/1988

Ms. Schmidt is now 33, treated last fall for intrauterine adhesions and since followed by endocrinology for a small prolactinoma on cabergoline. Over the past 6 months her cycles first came closer together, from every 28 days down to about every 21, and then stopped altogether; no bleeding at all for 3 months. Still no pregnancy. She has not had hot flashes, sweats at night, or vaginal dryness.

Her thyroid disease is well controlled on levothyroxine.
FH: no relatives with early menopause that she knows of. A brother had a learning disability and behavior problems from a young age.
Allergies: NKDA.

FSH 108 mIU/mL (3.5-12.5)

Estradiol 20 pg/mL (30-400)
TSH 2.5
Free T4 1.2 ng/dL (0.8-1.8)

documents.title: Question about cabergoline
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, quick question. At my gyn appointment last month my prolactin was normal (14), so I stopped the cabergoline about two weeks ago. I figured if it's normal I don't need it? I haven't seen the endocrinologist since last year. Is that ok?

documents.title: RE: Question about cabergoline
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wendy. A normal prolactin on cabergoline usually means the medicine is doing its job, not that the tumor is gone, and prolactin can climb back up once it's stopped. The decision about stopping really belongs with your endocrinologist, who may want a recheck and an MRI first. Please call her office this week and tell them you've stopped. If the milky discharge comes back, or you notice headaches or vision changes, let us know.

Progressive headaches and reduced peripheral vision

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: headaches

HPI: 34F with prolactinoma, POI and Hashimoto. Endocrinology letter from August in chart: prolactin 250 after she stopped cabergoline on her own; they restarted it and ordered a repeat MRI. That MRI never got scheduled (she says no one called and she didn't chase it). Back on cabergoline since August.

Headaches: temples, most days now, worse over the last two months. And something new over about two months: she keeps being startled by people and cars that appear at her sides. No double vision. No nausea or vomiting. No weakness or numbness.

Still no periods. Some milky discharge persists.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, appropriate. Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Fundi: discs sharp bilaterally. Face symmetric, strength and sensation intact, gait normal.

A/P:
1. Prolactinoma with progressive headaches and symptoms suggesting loss of side vision. Concern for growth. MRI pituitary with and without contrast ordered here, marked to be done in the next few weeks, rather than waiting on the old order. Neurology referral placed for the headaches and a formal field assessment. Messaged endocrinology about the visit.
2. Cabergoline back on the list (0.25 mg twice weekly, endocrinology).
3. No driving at night or in unfamiliar areas until her vision is assessed; she agreed.
4. TSH today.
Call with any sudden severe headache or sudden vision loss: go to the ED.

documents.title: MRI and referral scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: MRI pituitary approved by insurance, scheduled 1/16/24 at the outside imaging center (earliest with contrast and pituitary protocol). Neurology new consult 1/23/24. Pt informed. TSH from 12/5 normal per PCP, pt told.

reports.study: MR Pituitary and Sella turcica WO and W contrast IV
reports.text:
Indication: known prolactinoma; worsening headaches, peripheral vision complaints. Comparison: 2/8/2022.
Technique: sagittal and coronal T1, coronal T2, pre- and post-gadolinium imaging of the sella, with dynamic coronal post-contrast series.
Findings: The previously described left pituitary lesion has enlarged and now forms a 1.5 cm sellar mass measured in greatest craniocaudal dimension, extending upward out of the sella. Its superior margin elevates and compresses the optic chiasm. The pituitary stalk is displaced slightly to the right. No hemorrhage within the mass. Cavernous sinuses are symmetric and the internal carotid flow voids are preserved. The visualized brain parenchyma, ventricles and extra-axial spaces are normal.
reports.conclusion: Interval enlargement of the pituitary adenoma, now a 1.5 cm macroadenoma compressing the optic chiasm.

documents.title: MRI pituitary
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Outside imaging center: MRI pituitary with and without contrast 1/16/2024, ordered by PCP. Impression: interval enlargement of pituitary adenoma, now 1.5 cm, compressing the optic chiasm. Critical finding called to the ordering office at 09:35.

documents.title: MRI result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with MRI: adenoma is larger, about 1.5 cm, pressing on the optic nerves where they cross, which fits her side-vision symptoms. Spoke directly with her endocrinologist, who will see her within the next few weeks and wants her to keep taking cabergoline in the meantime; neurology appointment next Tuesday stands. Reviewed warning signs (sudden severe headache, sudden worse vision, vomiting, confusion) that mean the ED. She asked good questions, husband on speaker. Not driving.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Visit date: 1/23/2024
Referred by: primary care

History: 35-year-old woman under endocrinology care for a prolactinoma, with ongoing galactorrhea and amenorrhea, referred for headaches that have been building over 3 months together with shrinking peripheral vision. Her periods are irregular, and milk still leaks from both breasts without any squeezing. She is not pregnant and has never taken hormonal birth control.
ROS: no weight change. No recent stress.
Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily (cabergoline per patient, managed by endocrinology). Allergies: NKDA.

Examination: alert and fully oriented, language and memory normal. Visual fields to confrontation show loss of the temporal field in each eye, a bitemporal hemianopia. Acuity grossly preserved. Pupils reactive without an afferent defect. Remaining cranial nerves normal. Strength, tone, reflexes, coordination and gait normal.

Data: prolactin today 125 ng/mL. MRI pituitary of 1/16/2024 personally reviewed: 1.5 cm sellar mass compressing the optic chiasm.

Impression: macroprolactinoma with chiasmal compression causing bitemporal hemianopia; headaches attributable to the mass.

Recommendations: discussed with her endocrinologist today, who will see her early February to adjust treatment. Formal perimetry through ophthalmology. Return to the ED for sudden headache or acute visual decline. Neurology follow-up as needed.

cc: PCP, endocrinology

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group
Follow-up 2/6/2024

Prolactinoma has grown to 1.5 cm with chiasmal compression and a bitemporal field defect (neurology 1/23). Prolactin 125 on cabergoline 0.25 mg twice weekly, restarted in August. Headaches unchanged. Taking it reliably now, she says.

Plan:
1. Increase cabergoline to 0.5 mg (one full tablet) twice weekly. Medical therapy remains first line even with chiasmal compression; most tumors shrink and fields recover. Surgery would be reconsidered if vision worsens or there is no response.
2. Pregnancy should be avoided until the tumor shrinks away from the chiasm, since these tumors can grow in pregnancy. Recommend a combined estrogen-progestin pill, which also gives her the estrogen her ovaries are not making. Asked her PCP to prescribe.
3. Formal visual fields at ophthalmology, already booked for 2/20.
4. MRI and prolactin in 5 to 6 months.

Allergies: NKDA. cc: PCP

Endocrinology (2/6 letter) increased cabergoline to 0.5 mg twice weekly and asked us to start a combined pill: avoid pregnancy while the macroadenoma shrinks, and replace estrogen for her ovarian insufficiency. Hard conversation for her after years of trying, but she understands the reasoning and wants to follow it.

Screening for estrogen: never smoker, no migraine with aura (her headaches are the tumor kind, no aura), no personal or family history of clots, no liver disease, no breast cancer history. Home BP readings this week 112/70 to 118/76.

Plan:
- Start drospirenone 3 mg / ethinyl estradiol 0.02 mg, one daily, starting Sunday. Spotting the first months is common. Reviewed clot warning signs.
- Cabergoline list updated to 0.5 mg twice weekly.
- Field testing at ophthalmology next week.
- Folic acid: fine to continue.
Will plan to see her for her physical in the fall.

reports.study: MR Pituitary and Sella turcica WO and W contrast IV
reports.text:
Indication: macroprolactinoma on cabergoline. Comparison: 1/16/2024.
Technique: standard pituitary protocol before and after IV gadolinium.
Findings: The pituitary adenoma has decreased in size, now measuring 8 mm in greatest dimension and confined to the sella. The optic chiasm is no longer contacted and is normal in position and signal. The stalk is midline. Cavernous sinuses are unremarkable. No hemorrhage.
reports.conclusion: Marked interval decrease of the pituitary adenoma, now 8 mm, with no contact with the optic chiasm.

documents.title: MRI pituitary

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group
Follow-up 7/23/2024

Doing well. Headaches resolved by spring. Says her side vision feels normal again.
Ophthalmology: perimetry in February confirmed bitemporal field loss; repeat perimetry in July is full in both eyes.
MRI 7/16: adenoma 8 mm, away from the chiasm.
Prolactin today 19 ng/mL.
Meds: cabergoline 0.5 mg twice weekly; drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol daily; levothyroxine 75 mcg.

Assessment: macroprolactinoma responding well to cabergoline, fields recovered.
Plan: continue cabergoline 0.5 mg twice weekly and the pill. Prolactin in 6 months, and then we can talk about timing for pregnancy.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First full physical since 2022 (spring 2023 cancelled, and the winter was all about the pituitary).

Pituitary: endocrinology's July note in chart. Tumor down to 8 mm, off the chiasm, prolactin 19, perimetry normal. No headaches. Vision normal to her. Cabergoline 0.5 mg twice weekly.
On the pill since February, regular withdrawal bleeds, no side effects. Plans to revisit pregnancy with endocrinology in January.
Thyroid fine. Eating well, weight steady.
Mood: better than last year by a lot. PHQ-9 3.

Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, cabergoline 0.5 mg twice weekly, drospirenone/EE daily, folic acid 0.4 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Thyroid normal. Breasts deferred to gyn. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Pelvic: speculum exam, normal cervix, Pap with HPV collected. Skin normal. Neuro nonfocal.

Plan:
- Pap with HPV today (last 2018).
- CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH.
- Flu and 2024-25 COVID today.
- Continue current meds.
Physical next fall.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Everything from Tuesday is normal: Pap and HPV negative, so the next one is in 5 years. Cholesterol, blood counts, kidney and liver tests and thyroid all fine.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group
Follow-up 1/21/2025

Well, no headaches, no visual symptoms, no galactorrhea. On cabergoline 0.5 mg twice weekly, combined pill, levothyroxine.
Prolactin today 11 ng/mL.

Assessment: macroprolactinoma, well controlled; 8 mm and clear of the chiasm on the July MRI.

Plan: with good shrinkage and normal prolactin she may stop the combined pill and try to conceive. Continue cabergoline until a positive pregnancy test, then stop it and call us the same week; we'd follow symptoms and fields through any pregnancy. Prolactin and MRI in a year if not pregnant before then. Her ovarian insufficiency means conception may be difficult; she is aware and in touch with gynecology.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Gynecology follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY PRACTICE - PROGRESS NOTE (faxed on request)
Date of service: 07/25/2025
Re: Wendy Schmidt, DOB 12/16/1988
Dx: lactational amenorrhea

36-year-old with Hashimoto thyroiditis on levothyroxine and anorexia nervosa in remission, previously treated for intrauterine adhesions, a prolactinoma and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, back for menstrual irregularity. For 6 months, since coming off her oral contraceptive, cycles have been irregular and she has not conceived. Bleeding is coming less often and is lighter. No galactorrhea, no hirsutism. She describes more stress at work and has lost 5 kg over the last 3 months without trying. She says her eating disorder has been under better control over the past year.

Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BMI 18.5. Appears cachectic. Pelvic exam without abnormality.

Labs: FSH low, LH low, estradiol low. Prolactin normal. TSH normal, free T4 normal.

Assessment: secondary amenorrhea with low gonadotropins and estradiol in the setting of weight loss and stress.
Plan: weight restoration discussed; follow up with PCP regarding weight; return in 3 months.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, and to talk about weight.

Gynecology note from July finally arrived 10/28: cycles irregular since stopping the pill in January, low FSH, LH and estradiol with normal prolactin and thyroid, 5 kg weight loss over 3 months, BMI 18.5. (Their diagnosis line says "lactational amenorrhea.")

Weight here: 56.2 at intake in 2019, steady for years, 55.4 in April, 50.4 at gyn in July, 50.9 today. She says the summer was the most stressful stretch of her career and she often skipped lunch and ate late. She knows that pattern from her teens and says she caught it. Over the past two months she has been eating three meals most days. Denies purging, laxatives or over-exercising. No fear of eating, she says, more no time and no appetite under stress. Still hoping for a pregnancy, still no positive tests.

Mood: stressed, tired, not hopeless. PHQ-9 6.
Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg, cabergoline 0.5 mg twice weekly, folic acid. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Thin. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without lanugo; no parotid enlargement. Extremities warm.

A/P
1. Unintentional weight loss with her history of anorexia nervosa; weight up slightly from July. Referral to a dietitian with eating-disorder experience; she accepted. CBC, CMP, TSH today. Recheck weight at a nurse visit in January.
2. Secondary amenorrhea with low gonadotropins, per gynecology; likely tied to the weight change. Gyn following.
3. Prolactinoma: stable, endocrinology.
4. Hashimoto: TSH.
5. Flu vaccine today. She'll get her COVID dose at the pharmacy.
Physical next fall.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your labs from Friday are all normal: blood count, chemistries, protein levels and thyroid. The nutrition referral has been sent; their office will call you to schedule.

reports.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal imaging. Uterus anteverted and normal in size and contour; endometrium thin and uniform. No intrauterine gestational sac. Both ovaries visualized, normal in appearance. No adnexal mass. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Normal empty uterus. No sonographic evidence of intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival: 01/26/2026 05:40
Patient: Wendy Schmidt, 37F
Allergies: NKDA
Home meds (per patient list): levothyroxine 75 mcg daily
PMH (from shared record): Asherman syndrome; prolactinoma; hypergonadotropic hypogonadism; lactational amenorrhea (07/2025); Hashimoto thyroiditis; anorexia nervosa, in remission

HPI: has not been able to pass urine since last evening despite a strong urge; lower belly increasingly uncomfortable. She is convinced she is pregnant: several weeks of morning nausea, her abdomen getting bigger, sore breasts. Home pregnancy tests have been negative and she believes they are wrong. Has been trying to conceive for a year since stopping oral contraceptives. Infertility and prolactinoma history; seen for amenorrhea about six months ago. No fever, flank pain, back pain, leg weakness or numbness, no saddle numbness, no new medications.

Exam: anxious, tearful at times. Abdomen distended, with suprapubic fullness. Handheld fetal heart monitor: no fetal heart tones. Bimanual exam: uterus not enlarged, no adnexal mass. Breasts enlarged and tender to her, no galactorrhea. Back without tenderness. Lower extremity strength, sensation and reflexes normal; perineal sensation intact.

ED course: bedside bladder scan 850 mL. Straight catheterization drained 800 mL of clear urine with immediate relief. Urine hCG negative. Serum hCG <5 mIU/mL. TSH 2.5 uIU/mL (0.4-4.0). Prolactin 14 ng/mL (4-23). BMP normal. Urinalysis normal. Pelvic ultrasound: normal empty uterus, no intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy. Results reviewed with her at length; she was distressed but accepted them by the end of the visit. Voided on her own twice before discharge, comfortable.

Diagnosis: psychogenic urinary retention due to acute stress reaction.

Disposition: discharged home with her husband. Follow up with primary care this week and with outpatient behavioral health; resource list given. Return for inability to void, fever, back pain, or leg weakness.

cc: primary care physician

documents.title: ER visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: You probably got the ER papers. I'm ok now. I'm honestly embarrassed about it. I really thought I was pregnant. Things are better, I'm peeing normally and I've talked a lot with my husband. I don't think I need to come in right now, I'll see you at my physical.

documents.title: RE: ER visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Wendy, thank you for writing, and there is nothing to be embarrassed about. Your body and mind have been through a great deal with all of this. I did read the ER record. I'd still be glad to see you sooner than the fall, even just a short visit or a video call to talk about how you're doing and about a counselor; the ER suggested one, and I agree it could help. You can book anytime. If the trouble passing urine ever comes back, go back to the ER.
